clocks.name: California, sample copy of the breach notification to the Attorney General (more than 500 residents)
clocks.trigger: notifying affected consumers of a breach that requires notice to more than 500 California residents
clocks.deadline_text: shall electronically submit a single sample copy of that security breach notification, excluding any personally identifiable information, to the Attorney General within 15 calendar days of notifying affected consumers of the security breach
clocks.notes: Opened in the desktop browser pane on 2026-11-03. The clock runs from the date consumers are notified, not from discovery. Submitted through the Attorney General's online breach reporting form (https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/databreach/reporting, also opened on 2026-11-03).

clocks.name: California licensed health facility report of unlawful or unauthorized access
clocks.trigger: detection of unlawful or unauthorized access to, or use or disclosure of, a patient's medical information
clocks.deadline_text: report to the department and the affected patient no later than 15 business days after the unlawful or unauthorized access, use, or disclosure has been detected
clocks.notes: source not fetched; verify before use. leginfo.legislature.ca.gov returned 403 to the automated fetch on 2026-11-03, so the wording is from the drafter's reading of the statute and must be checked by a human.

clocks.name: California, notice of a data breach to affected residents
clocks.trigger: discovery or notification of a breach of the security of the system involving unencrypted personal information of a California resident
clocks.deadline_text: the disclosure required by this subdivision shall be made within 30 calendar days of discovery or notification of the data breach
clocks.notes: Opened in the desktop browser pane on 2026-11-03 (WebFetch returned 403). The page text read on 2026-11-03 contains a 30 calendar day limit at 1798.82(a)(2)(A); older summaries describe only the open-ended 'most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' standard, so this is a recent amendment and a human should confirm its effective date. Disclosure may be delayed for the legitimate needs of law enforcement (subdivision (c)) or as necessary to determine the scope of the breach and restore integrity (subdivision (a)(2)(B)).

clocks.name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, notice to the Secretary (500 or more individuals)
clocks.trigger: discovery of a breach of unsecured PHI involving 500 or more individuals
clocks.deadline_text: contemporaneously with the notice required by 164.404(a), without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery
clocks.notes: Text confirmed via law.cornell.edu mirror on 2026-11-03. Filed through the HHS breach portal. Breaches under 500 are logged and reported within 60 days after the end of the calendar year (164.408(c)).

clocks.name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, notice to individuals
clocks.trigger: discovery of a breach of unsecured protected health information
clocks.deadline_text: without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery of a breach
clocks.notes: Text confirmed via law.cornell.edu mirror on 2026-11-03. The 60 days is an outer limit; the standard is without unreasonable delay. Discovery is the first day the breach is known or should reasonably have been known (164.404(a)(2)). A breach is presumed unless the four-factor risk assessment in 164.402 shows a low probability of compromise.

clocks.name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, notice to prominent media outlets
clocks.trigger: discovery of a breach of unsecured PHI involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
clocks.deadline_text: without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery of a breach
clocks.notes: Text confirmed via law.cornell.edu mirror on 2026-11-03. The threshold is more than 500 residents of a single state or jurisdiction, not 500 individuals in total; the engine approximates with the total affected estimate and the facilitator should confirm the per-state count.

source_documents.title: Valley Regional Health System Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan

items.label: Incident Commander
items.value: Chief Information Security Officer; declares incidents, assigns severity, activates the CIRT, directs containment
items.quote: The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) serves as Incident Commander for all cybersecurity incidents.

items.label: Incident declaration and severity
items.value: Incident Commander
items.quote: The Incident Commander has the authority to declare a cybersecurity incident, assign its severity level, activate the Cyber Incident Response Team, and direct containment actions.

items.label: Director of Security Operations
items.value: Deputy Incident Commander; runs detection and containment actions
items.quote: When the CISO is unavailable, the Director of Security Operations serves as Incident Commander.

items.label: Shutdown or isolation of a production clinical system
items.value: Chief Information Officer, after consulting the Chief Medical Information Officer
items.quote: The Chief Information Officer (CIO) authorizes the shutdown or isolation of any production clinical system, including the electronic health record, after consulting the Chief Medical Information Officer.

items.label: Chief Information Officer
items.value: Authorizes clinical system shutdown and the restore order
items.quote: The Chief Information Officer (CIO) authorizes the shutdown or isolation of any production clinical system, including the electronic health record, after consulting the Chief Medical Information Officer.

items.label: SEV1 emergency isolation notice to the CIO
items.value: Incident Commander may isolate immediately in SEV1 and must tell the CIO within 30 minutes
items.quote: In a SEV1 incident the Incident Commander may isolate a system immediately and must notify the CIO within 30 minutes of doing so.

items.label: Privacy Officer
items.value: Owns the breach risk assessment and the reportable-breach decision with General Counsel
items.quote: The Privacy Officer owns the breach risk assessment and decides, with General Counsel, whether an incident is a reportable breach of protected health information.

items.label: Reportable breach determination
items.value: Privacy Officer with General Counsel
items.quote: The Privacy Officer owns the breach risk assessment and decides, with General Counsel, whether an incident is a reportable breach of protected health information.

items.label: General Counsel
items.value: Only role that speaks to regulators, law enforcement, and the cyber insurer
items.quote: General Counsel is the only role authorized to communicate with regulators, law enforcement, and the cyber insurance carrier on behalf of VRHS.

items.label: Public statements, patient notifications, media response
items.value: Chief Executive Officer on the recommendation of the Director of Communications and General Counsel
items.quote: The Chief Executive Officer approves any public statement, patient-facing notification, or media response, on the recommendation of the Director of Communications and General Counsel.

items.label: Chief Executive Officer
items.value: Approves public statements and patient notifications; informs the Board Chair
items.quote: The Chief Executive Officer approves any public statement, patient-facing notification, or media response, on the recommendation of the Director of Communications and General Counsel.

items.label: Director of Communications
items.value: Drafts every external statement and workforce update
items.quote: All external statements, including holding statements to the media, are drafted by the Director of Communications, reviewed by General Counsel, and approved by the Chief Executive Officer before release.

items.label: SEV1 (Critical)
items.value: Clinical system, PHI system, or Active Directory compromised or unavailable, or any ransomware detonation; requires Hospital Command Center activation
items.quote: SEV1 (Critical): confirmed compromise or loss of availability of a clinical system, a system containing protected health information, or the identity infrastructure (Active Directory), or any ransomware detonation.

items.label: SEV2 (High)
items.value: Non-clinical business system compromise, a compromised privileged account, or suspected PHI access without loss of availability
items.quote: SEV2 (High): confirmed compromise of a non-clinical business system, a compromised privileged account, or suspected unauthorized access to protected health information without confirmed loss of availability.

items.label: Severity assignment and re-rating
items.value: Incident Commander assigns at declaration and may change it; every change logged with time and reason
items.quote: The Incident Commander assigns the severity level at declaration and may raise or lower it as facts develop.

items.label: Security Operations to Incident Commander
items.value: Within 15 minutes of identifying a suspected SEV1 or SEV2
items.quote: Security Operations notifies the Incident Commander within 15 minutes of identifying a suspected SEV1 or SEV2 incident.

items.label: Incident Commander to CIO and Privacy Officer
items.value: Within 30 minutes of declaring SEV1 or SEV2
items.quote: The Incident Commander notifies the CIO and the Privacy Officer within 30 minutes of declaring a SEV1 or SEV2 incident.

items.label: CIO to CEO and General Counsel
items.value: Within 1 hour of a SEV1 declaration
items.quote: The CIO notifies the Chief Executive Officer and General Counsel within 1 hour of a SEV1 declaration.

items.label: CEO to Board Chair
items.value: Within 24 hours of a SEV1 declaration
items.quote: The Chief Executive Officer informs the Board Chair within 24 hours of a SEV1 declaration.

items.label: Hospital Command Center activation
items.value: Incident Commander requests activation through the Emergency Management Director for any SEV1
items.quote: For any SEV1 incident, the Incident Commander requests activation of the Hospital Command Center through the Emergency Management Director.

items.label: Clinical downtime procedures
items.value: Activated by the Chief Nursing Officer for affected units
items.quote: Clinical downtime procedures are activated by the Chief Nursing Officer for affected units.

items.label: Cyber insurance carrier notice
items.value: General Counsel, within 24 hours of a SEV1 or SEV2 declaration and before any outside firm is engaged
items.quote: General Counsel notifies the cyber insurance carrier within 24 hours of a SEV1 or SEV2 declaration and before any outside forensic firm, breach counsel, or negotiator is engaged.

items.label: FBI notification
items.value: General Counsel decides; expected for ransomware and any exfiltration
items.quote: Notification is expected for any ransomware incident and any incident with evidence of data exfiltration.

items.label: Four-factor breach risk assessment
items.value: Privacy Officer completes it within 10 business days of confirmed unauthorized PHI access
items.quote: The Privacy Officer completes the four-factor breach risk assessment within 10 business days of the Incident Commander confirming that protected health information was accessed, acquired, used, or disclosed without authorization.

items.label: Individual notification internal standard
items.value: 45 calendar days from discovery, stricter than the regulatory 60
items.quote: VRHS's internal standard is to issue individual notifications within 45 calendar days of discovery, which is stricter than the regulatory outer limit.

items.label: Notification ownership
items.value: General Counsel owns regulatory notices; Privacy Officer owns individual letters
items.quote: General Counsel owns the regulatory notifications and the Privacy Officer owns the individual notification letters.

items.label: Evidence before rebuild
items.value: Forensic image captured or confirmed before any affected system is rebuilt or restored
items.quote: Before any affected system is rebuilt or restored, Security Operations captures a forensic image or confirms that the outside forensic firm has done so.

items.label: Standard containment actions
items.value: Isolate, disable compromised accounts, reset privileged and service credentials used in the last 30 days, block attacker infrastructure
items.quote: Security Operations isolates the affected system from the network, disables compromised accounts, resets credentials for all privileged and service accounts that authenticated to the affected system in the preceding 30 days, and blocks the attacker infrastructure at the perimeter.

items.label: Medical device isolation
items.value: Director of Clinical Engineering isolates devices and confirms downtime procedures with nursing
items.quote: The Director of Clinical Engineering isolates affected medical devices and confirms with nursing leadership that patient care has moved to downtime procedures.

items.label: EHR recovery objectives
items.value: RTO 4 hours, RPO 15 minutes
items.quote: The electronic health record has a recovery time objective of 4 hours and a recovery point objective of 15 minutes.

items.label: Active Directory recovery objective
items.value: RTO 2 hours
items.quote: Active Directory has a recovery time objective of 2 hours.

items.label: Restore order
items.value: Active Directory, network services, EHR and interface engine, ancillary clinical systems, business systems; CIO may change it with CMIO agreement
items.quote: Systems are restored in this order: identity infrastructure (Active Directory), network services, the electronic health record and its interface engine, ancillary clinical systems, and then business systems.

items.label: Backup validation before restore
items.value: Backup must predate the earliest known compromise and have a successful test restore
items.quote: Before restoring from backup, the Director of Infrastructure confirms that the backup predates the earliest known compromise and that a test restore of the backup has completed successfully.

items.label: Ransomware step 1: isolate and preserve
items.value: Security Operations isolates affected systems and preserves the ransom note and attacker communication
items.quote: Step 1. Security Operations isolates affected systems and preserves the ransom note and any attacker communication as evidence.

items.label: Ransomware step 2: declare SEV1
items.value: Incident Commander declares SEV1 and requests Hospital Command Center activation
items.quote: Step 2. The Incident Commander declares a SEV1 incident and requests Hospital Command Center activation.

items.label: Ransomware step 3: verify backups
items.value: Director of Infrastructure verifies backups are offline and unaffected
items.quote: Step 3. The Director of Infrastructure verifies that backups are offline and unaffected.

items.label: Ransomware step 4: insurer and FBI
items.value: General Counsel notifies the cyber insurance carrier and the FBI field office
items.quote: Step 4. General Counsel notifies the cyber insurance carrier and the FBI field office.

items.label: Ransomware step 5: reset credentials and rebuild identity
items.value: Security Operations resets all privileged credentials and rebuilds identity infrastructure from a known-good state
items.quote: Step 5. Security Operations resets all privileged credentials and rebuilds the identity infrastructure from a known-good state.

items.label: Ransomware step 6: CIO approves restore order
items.value: CIO approves the restore order under section 7.2
items.quote: Step 6. The CIO approves the restore order under section 7.2.

items.label: Ransomware step 7: breach risk assessment
items.value: Privacy Officer begins the breach risk assessment under section 5.1
items.quote: Step 7. The Privacy Officer begins the breach risk assessment under section 5.1.

items.label: Workforce notice template
items.value: Director of Communications, every 4 hours in SEV1, reviewed by the Incident Commander
items.quote: The Director of Communications issues workforce updates at least every 4 hours during a SEV1 incident using the pre-approved workforce notice template, after review by the Incident Commander.

items.label: Holding statement template and approval chain
items.value: Drafted by Communications, reviewed by General Counsel, approved by the CEO
items.quote: All external statements, including holding statements to the media, are drafted by the Director of Communications, reviewed by General Counsel, and approved by the Chief Executive Officer before release.

items.label: Patient-facing notices about delayed or diverted care
items.value: Approved by the Chief Medical Officer and the Chief Executive Officer
items.quote: Patient-facing notices about delayed or diverted care are approved by the Chief Medical Officer and the Chief Executive Officer.

items.label: Incident log
items.value: Incident Commander logs the time of every decision, who made it, and who was notified
items.quote: The Incident Commander maintains the incident log, including the time of every decision, who made it, and who was notified.

items.label: Discovery date for business associate incidents
items.value: The date VRHS was notified by the business associate
items.quote: the Privacy Officer confirms that the business associate agreement's notification clause was met and records the date VRHS was notified as the discovery date.

gaps.topic: Ransom payment decision and attacker communication
gaps.note: The plan names no role authorized to decide whether to pay a ransom or to communicate with the attacker. Section 8 preserves the ransom note as evidence but is silent on negotiation and payment authority, sanctions screening, and insurer consent.
The plan does not say who decides to place the emergency department on EMS diversion during a cyber incident or how that decision reaches EMS partners and neighboring hospitals.

The plan sets an internal 45-day standard for individual notices but is silent on the California Department of Public Health report, which the healthcare pack lists at 15 business days from detection.
The plan covers workforce updates and media statements but says nothing about staff posting about the incident on social media.

ground_rules: This is a discussion, not a test of individuals. There are no wrong answers, only decisions and their consequences.
Respond as you would today with the plans, people, and tools you actually have, not the ones you wish you had.
The facilitator controls the clock. When the facilitator says time has passed, it has.
Decisions are recorded as the team states them. Say who decided and who was told.
Nothing discussed here is a finding against any person. The after-action report labels gaps in plans, roles, and technology.
Phones down unless you are playing the role of the person being called.
objectives: Exercise the organization's own written procedures under a scenario built from its own exposure data.
Confirm who holds each decision and whether the escalation path works at speed.
Test the notification clocks that apply to this organization and who owns each one.
Find the points where the plan is silent, contradictory, or unknown to the people who must use it.
Produce a scored after-action report with owners and dates for every gap.

injects.title: First signal on vpngw01
injects.what_happens: The security tool flags repeated authentication failures and a new administrative session on vpngw01, the internet-facing system that carries CVE-2025-0282. The analyst on shift is not sure whether it is a scan or a compromise.
injects.decision_forced: Is this an incident, who gets told right now, and what severity does the analyst assign?

procedure_tested.label: IR Plan section 4.1 Security Operations to Incident Commander
procedure_tested.quote: Security Operations notifies the Incident Commander within 15 minutes of identifying a suspected SEV1 or SEV2 incident.

injects.what_good_looks_like: The analyst confirms the alert with a second source, opens an incident record with a timeline, and escalates to the incident lead within the time the plan commits to, citing vpngw01 by name.
injects.where_teams_fail: The analyst waits for more evidence, the alert sits in a queue, and nobody records when it was first seen.

expected_actions.text: Within 15 minutes of identifying a suspected SEV1 or SEV2
Confirm the alert with a second source (EDR, firewall, or help desk reports) before declaring
Open an incident record and start a timestamped timeline

hints: Ask who is on call tonight and how they are reached.
Ask what second source would confirm or clear the alert.
probing_questions: Who decides this is an incident, and does the analyst know that name?
What severity would you assign and what in the plan says so?
host_lines: It is a Tuesday evening. Your security tooling has raised an alert on vpngw01. The analyst has a screen full of failed logins and one that succeeded. What do you do in the next fifteen minutes?

injects.title: Declaring the incident
injects.what_happens: Evidence now shows the attacker holds an administrative session on vpngw01 and has reached the identity server dc1 by exploitation of CVE-2020-1472. The incident lead must decide whether to declare, at what severity, and who is called in.
injects.decision_forced: Declare the incident and set the severity; name who is notified and in what order.

procedure_tested.label: IR Plan section 8 Ransomware step 2: declare SEV1
procedure_tested.quote: Step 2. The Incident Commander declares a SEV1 incident and requests Hospital Command Center activation.

injects.what_good_looks_like: The incident lead declares the incident, assigns the severity the plan defines, and notifies leadership, counsel, and the cyber insurer in the order the plan sets (IR Plan section 8 Ransomware step 2: declare SEV1).
injects.where_teams_fail: Declaration is delayed to avoid alarming executives, counsel is not engaged, and the insurer is called after outside help has already been retained.

expected_actions.text: Incident Commander declares SEV1 and requests Hospital Command Center activation
Within 30 minutes of declaring SEV1 or SEV2
Within 1 hour of a SEV1 declaration

hints: Ask for the exact phrase the plan uses for the declaration.
probing_questions: What severity, and which sentence in the plan says so?
Who is on the notification list for this severity and who calls them?
host_lines: The attacker is on dc1. Is this an incident under your plan? Say the severity out loud and tell me who you are calling, in order.

injects.title: Containment on dc1
injects.what_happens: Containment options are on the table: isolate vpngw01, reset every privileged credential, and take dc1 offline. Each option cuts a service the business is using right now. Then a second report contradicts the first: the vendor says vpngw01 was patched last month and the alert is a false positive, while the forensics lead says the patch was never applied.
injects.decision_forced: Which systems are isolated now, who authorizes it, and how is evidence preserved?

procedure_tested.label: IR Plan section 2.3 Shutdown or isolation of a production clinical system
procedure_tested.quote: The Chief Information Officer (CIO) authorizes the shutdown or isolation of any production clinical system, including the electronic health record, after consulting the Chief Medical Information Officer.

injects.what_good_looks_like: The team isolates the entry system, preserves images before rebuilding, resets privileged credentials, and names the person who authorized each action (IR Plan section 2.3 Shutdown or isolation of a production clinical system).
injects.where_teams_fail: The team reimages the entry system before forensics has a copy, or waits for a perfect picture while the attacker keeps moving.

expected_actions.text: Incident Commander may isolate immediately in SEV1 and must tell the CIO within 30 minutes
Isolate, disable compromised accounts, reset privileged and service credentials used in the last 30 days, block attacker infrastructure
Director of Clinical Engineering isolates devices and confirms downtime procedures with nursing

hints: Ask whether anyone has taken a forensic image yet.
Ask who can approve taking a production system offline.
probing_questions: Who authorizes the shutdown, and is that person in the room?
What are you doing to preserve evidence before you contain?
Two credible sources disagree. What do you do with containment while you find out which is right?
host_lines: Your team can isolate vpngw01 and dc1 right now. Doing so cuts remote access and authentication for the building. Who decides, and what do you say to the business?

injects.title: The business tradeoff
injects.what_happens: sql2016 is confirmed affected and the PHI and PII it holds may be exposed. Operations asks to keep the system running through the busiest hours of the day; security asks to take it down now. A ransom note has appeared on two systems.
injects.decision_forced: Keep the system up and accept the exposure, or take it down and accept the outage? Who makes that call?

procedure_tested.label: Plan is silent on: Ransom payment decision and attacker communication

injects.what_good_looks_like: The decision is made by the role the plan names, within minutes, with the reasons recorded, and the ransom question is routed to counsel and the insurer (Plan is silent on: Ransom payment decision and attacker communication).
injects.where_teams_fail: Nobody can name who holds the decision, so it drifts to whoever speaks loudest.

expected_actions.text: Security Operations isolates affected systems and preserves the ransom note and attacker communication
Security Operations resets all privileged credentials and rebuilds identity infrastructure from a known-good state
Activated by the Chief Nursing Officer for affected units

hints: Ask who signs the shutdown order.
Ask whether anyone has opened the ransom note's instructions.
probing_questions: Who holds this decision in your plan?
What is the plan's position on ransom payment, and who is allowed to talk to the attacker?
host_lines: A ransom note is on screen. sql2016 is affected. Operations wants to keep it running. Who decides, and what do they decide?

injects.title: Restore order for sql2016
injects.what_happens: Backups for sql2016 exist but the last successful restore test was months ago. The business wants sql2016 first; IT wants the identity systems first. Clinics and departments are working on paper until it is decided.
injects.decision_forced: What is restored first, who approves the order, and what is the recovery time objective you are now working to?

procedure_tested.label: IR Plan section 7.2 Restore order
procedure_tested.quote: Systems are restored in this order: identity infrastructure (Active Directory), network services, the electronic health record and its interface engine, ancillary clinical systems, and then business systems.

injects.what_good_looks_like: The team checks the backups are clean before restoring, agrees a restore order with the business owners, and states the recovery objective from the plan (IR Plan section 7.2 Restore order).
injects.where_teams_fail: The team restores from a backup that was never verified, or restores the crown jewel before the identity systems and loses it again.

expected_actions.text: Active Directory, network services, EHR and interface engine, ancillary clinical systems, business systems; CIO may change it with CMIO agreement
RTO 4 hours, RPO 15 minutes
RTO 2 hours

hints: Ask when the backup was last tested.

probing_questions: What is your recovery time objective for this system and where is it written?

injects.title: The notification clock starts
injects.what_happens: Counsel confirms that PHI and PII on sql2016 were accessed. The notification clocks start now. The tightest one belongs to California Department of Public Health: 15 business days.
injects.decision_forced: Which clocks apply, who owns each notification, and what is the first draft of the notice?

procedure_tested.quote: General Counsel owns the regulatory notifications and the Privacy Officer owns the individual notification letters.

injects.what_good_looks_like: The team lists every applicable clock with its owner and due date, starts the regulator notice, and records the discovery date it will defend (IR Plan section 5.2 Notification ownership).
injects.where_teams_fail: The team debates whether data was really taken instead of starting the clock, or assumes one notice covers every regulator.

45 calendar days from discovery, stricter than the regulatory 60

procedure_tested.quote: All external statements, including holding statements to the media, are drafted by the Director of Communications, reviewed by General Counsel, and approved by the Chief Executive Officer before release.
